open_points.subject: A1 scan under concurrent folder changes
open_points.text: Syncthing may change the folder during a scan, and a scan promises nothing about a file or folder that changes while it runs.
open_points.question: For each kind of concurrent change—content replacement, rename, deletion, creation, or a folder becoming unavailable—must the scan report the listed object, report its new state, omit it, or refuse the whole scan, and which status or refusal applies?
options: Use the folder listing as the snapshot of names and classify each listed entry from what can be opened later
Use each entry's state when it is opened, allowing omission or a new classification
Permit any result, including omission or whole-scan refusal
open_points.default_guess: Use the listing for names, classify from the no-follow open, omit entries that vanished before metadata, and refuse only when a non-ignored subfolder cannot be listed.

witness.initial: A folder listing contains ordinary file a.jpg.
events: Syncthing replaces a.jpg with different bytes after the listing but before the scanner reads it.
outcomes: The scan reports the source id and facts of the replacement.
The scan omits a.jpg or reports facts derived from the earlier directory entry.
witness.observer: The calling flow comparing scan results

open_points.subject: A1 ignored-name classification
open_points.text: A name is ignored at every level of the path when, after the letters A to Z are lowered and no other character is changed, it begins with an item of the imported `IGNORED_NAME_PREFIXES` constant, ends with an item of the imported `IGNORED_NAME_SUFFIXES` constant, or contains the imported `CONFLICT_COPY_MARK` constant, the mark of a Syncthing conflict copy (R0-14).
open_points.question: At which instant and from which representation is each path component tested when an entry is renamed during a scan: the folder-listing name, the name at open time, or both?
options: Judge only the name returned by the folder listing
Re-resolve and judge the current name when opening
Require both the listed and current names to be non-ignored
open_points.default_guess: Judge the exact relative name returned by the folder listing and never follow a rename to another name.

witness.initial: The listing contains an ordinary name photo.jpg.
events: Syncthing renames it to photo.sync-conflict-1.jpg before the scanner opens the listed path.
outcomes: The listed ordinary name remains eligible for this scan.
The current conflict-copy name is ignored and cannot be reported.

open_points.subject: A1 source_id population
open_points.text: Files with the same content are each reported, with the same source id.
open_points.question: Which reported statuses must carry a source id, and does the sentence include empty, oversized, unreadable, non-regular, or unsupported files whose full content may not have been read?
options: Every reported entry carries a source id whenever its bytes can be read
Only ready, placed, and published entries carry a source id
Every regular file, including rejected files, is fully hashed unless reading fails
open_points.default_guess: Hash fully read regular files and give source ids to ready, placed, published, empty, and unsupported observations, but use null when the file cannot safely be fully read.

witness.initial: Two oversized files have identical bytes.
outcomes: Both rejected observations contain the same source id.
Both are rejected before full hashing and have null source ids.

open_points.subject: A1 file opening
open_points.text: opened without following a link and without waiting, what it finds is not a regular file
open_points.question: What precisely does “without waiting” require, which operation or flag implements it, and what result applies when an open would block or the platform cannot provide that mode?
options: Use a nonblocking no-follow open and classify its result
Use an ordinary no-follow open; “without waiting” only means no retry
Refuse unsupported platforms or filesystems
open_points.default_guess: Use one no-follow open attempt with no retry; do not promise that the operating-system call itself cannot block.

open_points.subject: A3 prerequisite scan
open_points.text: One call delivers one photo, named by `name`, the relative path a scan reported, and `source_id`.
open_points.question: Must a new delivery prove that this exact name and source_id were returned by an earlier scan, or may it deliver any current file that a scan could report without retaining scan state?
options: An actual earlier scan result is required
Only current eligibility equivalent to a scan is required
An earlier scan is required only for new placements, not replays
open_points.default_guess: No retained scan result is required; validate the current file as a scan would.

witness.initial: A valid photo exists, but the caller has not invoked scan.
events: The authenticated caller submits its correct name and source_id directly to delivery.
outcomes: The photo is delivered because it is currently scan-eligible.
The request fails with NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT because no scan reported it.

open_points.subject: A3 failure precedence for non-regular files
open_points.text:
| 1 | `name` is not a file a scan could report: it is empty, absolute, unnormalised, climbs with `..`, is ignored at any level, is not a regular file or passes through a symbolic link | `NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT` |
| 2 | A1 orders 1 to 6 reject the file | the member with the value of the A1 reason |
open_points.question: When the requested path resolves to a non-regular entry, when does condition 1 produce NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT and when does A1 order 3 produce NOT_A_REGULAR_FILE?
options: Stable non-regular entries use NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT; only a race discovered after an initially regular listing uses NOT_A_REGULAR_FILE
Every non-regular entry uses NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT
Every safely opened non-regular entry uses NOT_A_REGULAR_FILE
open_points.default_guess: Use NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT if initial path validation finds a non-regular entry, and NOT_A_REGULAR_FILE only if a previously regular entry changes before the no-follow open.

witness.initial: The requested name identifies a directory inside the photo folder.
events: The caller requests delivery with a syntactically valid source_id.
outcomes: Condition 1 returns NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT.
A1 order 3 returns NOT_A_REGULAR_FILE.

open_points.subject: A3 failure precedence for symbolic-link races
open_points.text:
| 1 | `name` is not a file a scan could report: it is empty, absolute, unnormalised, climbs with `..`, is ignored at any level, is not a regular file or passes through a symbolic link | `NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT` |
| 2 | A1 orders 1 to 6 reject the file | the member with the value of the A1 reason |
open_points.question: If an ordinary path becomes a symbolic link during delivery, does it fail as NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT under condition 1 or UNREADABLE_FILE under A1 order 5, and at what check is the distinction made?
options: Any symbolic link discovered before reading gives NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT
A link already present at validation gives NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT; one introduced afterward gives UNREADABLE_FILE
Any post-listing link gives UNREADABLE_FILE
open_points.default_guess: Use NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT when path validation observes the link and UNREADABLE_FILE when a later no-follow open detects the race.

witness.initial: name refers to an ordinary regular file.
events: Another actor replaces the file with a symbolic link before it is opened.
outcomes: Delivery fails with NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT.
Delivery fails with UNREADABLE_FILE.

open_points.subject: A3 failed storage writes
open_points.text:
A photo that cannot be delivered is answered with status `failed` and one member of
   `= models.PlacementFailure`, and nothing is written except the project lock:
open_points.question: How can a record-write failure satisfy “nothing is written” when rule 6 requires the stored image to be written before the record; must the image and temporary files be rolled back, retained for retry, or treated as a crash-only state?
options: Delete the newly written image and every temporary file before returning failed
Retain the complete image without a record and weaken the nothing-written promise
Treat a record-write failure as an unreturned crash rather than a failed outcome
open_points.default_guess: Attempt rollback of a newly written image and temporary files before returning failed; if rollback cannot be guaranteed, do not promise that nothing was written.

witness.initial: No placement or stored image exists for the source.
events: Delivery successfully writes and renames the stored image.
outcomes: The call returns failed and the stored image remains, as required by image-before-record ordering.
The call returns failed only after deleting the stored image, as required by the nothing-written promise.
witness.observer: The caller and an operator inspecting the binary store

open_points.subject: A3 request-form refusal
open_points.text: A defect of that form or of the project id is refused as a whole request.
open_points.question: What exact defects count, which refusal code or transport response each produces, and whether validation stops at the first defect are not stated.
options: Use framework validation for missing, extra, or wrongly typed fields and a separate invalid-project-id response
Map every form or project-id defect to one explicit RefusalCode
Define a precedence table for individual request defects
open_points.default_guess: Reject missing, extra, or non-string fields and malformed project ids before connection lookup using one documented request-validation response.

open_points.subject: A3 name normalisation
open_points.text: `name` is not a file a scan could report: it is empty, absolute, unnormalised, climbs with `..`, is ignored at any level, is not a regular file or passes through a symbolic link
open_points.question: What exact spellings are “unnormalised,” including repeated separators, `.` components, trailing separators, backslashes, Unicode normalization, percent escapes, and platform-specific drive or root forms?
options: Require POSIX relative paths in exact lexical normal form with `/` separators
Normalize first and accept if the result stays inside the folder
Apply host-platform path normalization rules
open_points.default_guess: Require a nonempty POSIX relative path already in lexical normal form, reject backslashes, `.` and `..` components, repeated or trailing separators, roots, and drive forms, and leave Unicode code points unchanged.

open_points.subject: INV-01 Required tests
open_points.text: INV-01: after a scan, a placement, a repeated placement and a mark, the source folder holds the same files with the same bytes, modification times and modes (`test_no_operation_changes_the_source_folder`).
open_points.question: Does “a placement” mean the new one-photo delivery operation, and must the test exercise both a successful delivery and every failed-delivery branch that reads a source?
options: Replace placement with delivery and cover successful, replayed, and failed deliveries
Treat placement as a synonym for delivery
Test only the successful and replayed paths named here
open_points.default_guess: Rewrite the item to name successful, replayed, and representative failed deliveries explicitly.

open_points.subject: INV-02 Required tests
open_points.text: INV-02: an empty, absolute, unnormalised or parent-climbing name, an ignored name at any level, a folder, and a path through a symbolic link each fail with the NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT member of = models.PlacementFailure and add no file except the project lock (`test_a_name_a_scan_would_not_report_is_not_delivered`).
open_points.question: What test shows that a file which becomes ignored, non-regular, or linked after initial validation is not read, as required by the invariant's universal “reads only” claim?
options: Add race tests for replacement by a conflict name, directory, and symbolic link
Narrow INV-02 to validation of stable paths
State that concurrent changes are outside INV-02
open_points.default_guess: Add a race test using a controlled filesystem seam and assert that the replaced target's bytes are never opened or decoded.

witness.initial: A valid ordinary file passes initial name validation.
events: Before the content read, another actor replaces it with a symbolic link to a readable image.
outcomes: The linked image is read, while all currently listed stable-name examples still pass the Required test.
The no-follow read refuses the replacement and no linked bytes are read.
witness.observer: The source-folder owner and the calling flow

open_points.subject: INV-07 Required tests
open_points.text: INV-07: a replaced file is reported as a new `ready` photo while the earlier image and mark stay (`test_a_replaced_file_is_a_new_photo_and_the_first_delivery_stays`), and a removed file keeps its delivery (`test_removing_a_file_keeps_its_delivery`).
open_points.question: What must the tests assert about the earlier placement record itself, which INV-07 requires to remain unchanged but the item explicitly mentions only the image, mark, and an undefined “delivery”?
options: Assert the exact earlier placement record remains byte-for-byte unchanged
Define “delivery stays” as including the placement record, stored image, and mark
Narrow the invariant to only the artifacts currently asserted
open_points.default_guess: Explicitly assert that the earlier placement record, image, and mark all remain unchanged after replacement and removal.

open_points.subject: INV-19 Required tests
open_points.text: INV-19: delivering content that has no placement under the name of a conflict copy fails with the NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT member of = models.PlacementFailure, adds no file except the project lock and changes no existing file (`test_a_syncthing_conflict_copy_is_neither_offered_nor_placed`). Placed content replays when only a conflict copy still holds it (`test_placed_content_replays_when_only_a_conflict_copy_still_holds_it`), and an ordinary file with the content of a conflict copy is delivered (`test_an_ordinary_file_is_placed_when_a_conflict_copy_has_the_same_content`).
open_points.question: What test shows that a new placement never reads a file renamed to a conflict-copy name after validation or an ordinary request path replaced by a conflict copy during delivery?
options: Add controlled rename-race tests and assert the conflict-copy bytes are never read
Define INV-19 only for names already conflicting when the call begins
Rely on INV-02 and state that it witnesses INV-19 too
open_points.default_guess: Add a controlled race test that renames or substitutes the entry before open and asserts failure with no source read and no durable write.

witness.initial: An ordinary file with no placement is selected for delivery.
events: After name validation, Syncthing renames it to a conflict-copy name or replaces its path with a conflict copy.
outcomes: The conflict-copy bytes are used for a new placement.
The delivery refuses without reading the conflict copy.
witness.observer: The owner and the Portal binary-store operator

open_points.subject: INV-12 Required tests
open_points.text: INV-12: concurrent placements of one source answer one `placed` and otherwise `replayed`, and marks from separate processes with two `photo_id` values answer one `marked`, `replayed` for the same value and `publication_conflict` for the other (`test_concurrent_calls_leave_one_placement_and_one_mark`, `test_separate_processes_leave_one_mark`).
open_points.question: Does the placement part also have to run in separate processes to demonstrate the rule's across-process locking guarantee, and does “placements” mean deliveries?
options: Require separate-process concurrent deliveries and separate-process marks
Use threads for deliveries and processes only for marks
Narrow the invariant to the concurrency modes actually tested
open_points.default_guess: Require separate-process concurrent deliveries as well as marks and rename the action to delivery.

open_points.subject: A7 clock-read boundary
open_points.text:
Only a mark reads it, once, after the token, the request form and the identifiers are accepted and
   before the connection is examined or the project lock is taken.
open_points.question: Which identifiers must be accepted before the clock read, in what order, and do syntactically valid but unknown project_id, source_id, or photo_id values count as accepted?
options: Token, request shape, project_id syntax, source_id syntax, and photo_id syntax precede the clock; existence checks follow it
Only project_id and photo_id syntax precede the clock
All identifier syntax and existence checks precede the clock
open_points.default_guess: Validate the syntax and type of project_id, source_id, and photo_id before reading the clock; perform connection, placement, and mark existence checks afterward.

witness.initial: A mark request has a valid token and form but a malformed source_id.
events: The service handles the request using a counting clock.
outcomes: The request is refused before the clock and the count remains zero.
The clock is read once before the malformed source_id is refused.

open_points.subject: A7 timestamp serialization
open_points.text:
The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding, written in ISO 8601 form.
open_points.question: Which exact ISO 8601 representation is required: separator, fixed or omitted fractional digits, treatment of zero microseconds, and whether a `Z` or offset is forbidden?
options: Always `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffff` with no suffix
Use the language's default datetime ISO formatter, allowing omitted zero fractions
Write `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ` despite the offset-free model
open_points.default_guess: Use exactly `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffff` with six fractional digits and no zone suffix.

open_points.subject: INV-13 Required tests
open_points.text: INV-13: a counting clock is read once by a mark and not at all by a scan, a delivery or the health answer (`test_only_the_mark_reads_the_clock`), and `marked_at` equals that reading (`test_a_marked_photo_is_reported_as_published`).
open_points.question: Which tests show zero reads for every pre-clock refusal and exactly one read for post-clock refusals and replayed marks, as the normative rule requires?
options: Add cases for each validation boundary, an unknown connection or placement, a replay, and a publication conflict
Test only one successful mark because the invariant says at most once
Narrow the normative rule to the successful path currently witnessed
open_points.default_guess: Add representative pre-clock and post-clock refusals plus replay and conflict cases, asserting exact read counts.

open_points.subject: context evidence for Syncthing
open_points.text:
Evidence is from local runs against a real Client Portal process and a stub Registry. No
run has used a live Syncthing folder, the kernel or the VPS.
open_points.question: How does this agree with R0-15's statement that “A run against real Syncthing” occurred and State 1's evidence naming `e2e_local_syncthing.py` with two private Syncthing instances; does “live” mean production/owner data rather than a real Syncthing process?
options: Change “live Syncthing folder” to “the owner's or production Syncthing folders”
Remove the claim that a real Syncthing run occurred
Define private test instances as not live and say so explicitly
open_points.default_guess: State that real isolated Syncthing processes were tested, but no owner's device, production folder, kernel, or VPS was used.

open_points.subject: A1 status and reason table
open_points.text:
| Order | Condition | Status | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | empty | `rejected` | `empty` |
| 2 | larger than the source limit | `rejected` | `too_large` |
| 3 | opened without following a link and without waiting, what it finds is not a regular file | `rejected` | `not_a_regular_file` |
| 4 | it grew past the source limit while being read | `rejected` | `too_large` |
| 5 | opening or reading it fails, which includes a file that disappeared and a path that became a symbolic link after the listing | `rejected` | `unreadable_file` |
| 6 | does not begin with a JPEG, PNG or WEBP signature | `rejected` | `unsupported_format` |
| 7 | placed and marked | `published` | none |
| 8 | placed | `placed` | none |
| 9 | anything else | `ready` | none |
open_points.rule:
**Член перечисления** note называет его именем рядом с адресом перечисления:
`the EXPENSE_CREATE member of = models.AuditAction`.
open_points.question: Replace each bare status and reason value with the emitted member name beside `= models.ScanStatus` or `= models.ObservationReason`; a wire value may appear only as an additional parenthetical value.

open_points.subject: A1 folder refusal
open_points.text:
When a subfolder that is not ignored
cannot be listed, the whole operation is refused with `folder_unavailable`, so a partial scan is
never reported as complete.
open_points.rule:
Имя — то, которое пишет
emitter моделей и которое получает генератор: имя из `member_names`, иначе
верхнее написание значения (`expense.create` → `EXPENSE_CREATE`, `pending` →
`PENDING`). Имя есть у каждого члена. Значение допустимо только как дополнение к
имени: `the EXPENSE_CREATE member (value expense.create) of = models.AuditAction`.
open_points.question: Name the FOLDER_UNAVAILABLE member of `= models.RefusalCode`, optionally adding its `folder_unavailable` value.

open_points.subject: A1 source-size policy
open_points.text: | 2 | larger than the source limit | `rejected` | `too_large` |
open_points.rule:
Таблица выше —
исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление
называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`,
настройка — полем объекта настроек.
open_points.question: Replace “the source limit” with “the imported MAX_SOURCE_BYTES constant” and name the enum members by emitted names.

open_points.subject: A1 growing-file policy
open_points.text: | 4 | it grew past the source limit while being read | `rejected` | `too_large` |
open_points.rule:
Таблица выше —
исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление
называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`,
настройка — полем объекта настроек.
open_points.question: Replace “the source limit” with “the imported MAX_SOURCE_BYTES constant” and name the enum members by emitted names.

open_points.subject: A3 replay outcome
open_points.text:
Delivering content that already has a placement answers `replayed` with the stored placement and the
   current `photo_id` of its mark, if any, and writes nothing, whatever name the request carries and even
   when the source file has left the folder.
open_points.rule:
Имя — то, которое пишет
emitter моделей и которое получает генератор: имя из `member_names`, иначе
верхнее написание значения (`expense.create` → `EXPENSE_CREATE`, `pending` →
`PENDING`). Имя есть у каждого члена. Значение допустимо только как дополнение к
имени: `the EXPENSE_CREATE member (value expense.create) of = models.AuditAction`.
open_points.question: Name the REPLAYED member of `= models.PlacementStatus`, optionally adding its `replayed` value.

open_points.subject: A3 malformed-source refusal
open_points.text:
A
   `source_id` that is not 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters is refused with `invalid_source_id`.
open_points.rule:
Имя — то, которое пишет
emitter моделей и которое получает генератор: имя из `member_names`, иначе
верхнее написание значения (`expense.create` → `EXPENSE_CREATE`, `pending` →
`PENDING`). Имя есть у каждого члена. Значение допустимо только как дополнение к
имени: `the EXPENSE_CREATE member (value expense.create) of = models.AuditAction`.
open_points.question: Name the INVALID_SOURCE_ID member of `= models.RefusalCode`, optionally adding its `invalid_source_id` value.

open_points.subject: A3 failed outcome
open_points.text:
A photo that cannot be delivered is answered with status `failed` and one member of
   `= models.PlacementFailure`, and nothing is written except the project lock:
open_points.rule:
Имя — то, которое пишет
emitter моделей и которое получает генератор: имя из `member_names`, иначе
верхнее написание значения (`expense.create` → `EXPENSE_CREATE`, `pending` →
`PENDING`). Имя есть у каждого члена. Значение допустимо только как дополнение к
имени: `the EXPENSE_CREATE member (value expense.create) of = models.AuditAction`.
open_points.question: Name the FAILED member of `= models.PlacementStatus`, optionally adding its `failed` value.

open_points.subject: A3 failure mapping
open_points.text:
| 2 | A1 orders 1 to 6 reject the file | the member with the value of the A1 reason |
| 3 | the hash of the bytes differs from `source_id` | `SOURCE_CHANGED` |
| 4 | A2 rule 2 fails | the member with the value of the A2 failure |
| 5 | writing the stored image or the record fails | `UNREADABLE_FILE` |
open_points.rule:
Член, названный одним значением, — нарушение: значение с точкой или дефисом не
является именем ни одного члена, генератор пишет только имена
(`AuditAction.EXPENSE_CREATE`), и валидатор отклоняет такую note
(`note_enum_member_by_value`).
open_points.question: Replace the value-based mappings with an exhaustive mapping that names every emitted member of `= models.PlacementFailure` explicitly.
